overall_reason: The cards carry specific facts ('Beta opens to every team on May 14.', '0.2s', 'Edits on the plane merge when you land.'), but the four headings are a feature-grid formula that holds for any document tool.

score.reason: T-THREE-LINE passes on '0.2s' and the offline-merge line; T-RIVAL-NAME on the headings and T-HEADING-FORM find four verb-phrase feature heads that would sit on any rival's page.

findings.evidence: The four headings read 'Write together', 'Find anything', 'Works offline' and 'Connects your tools'. Each stays true under any collaborative-docs competitor's name. 'Connects your tools' is followed by three blank squares, not named tools.
findings.after: Lead each card with its fact: name the integrations under 'Connects your tools' [DATA NEEDED: which tools], as the offline card does with 'Edits on the plane merge when you land.'
findings.why: Generic heads make the reader rely on the card bodies, and one card has no body to rely on.

strengths: 'Edits on the plane merge when you land.' explains offline sync with a concrete scene.
'Beta opens to every team on May 14.' is a dated fact.
not_investigated: T-LONG-FORM: no running-text region; the item is a single product composition with under 50 words.
